messages:
alex.m: Heads up — we rolled the kernel-selector + kvcache-prefetch experiment to canary at 02:15Z and I’m seeing p99 jump on canary -> spilling into prod. tagging @sam.r @anya

infra-bot: ANOMALY DETECTED: latency_p99 runtime-prod > 1.8s for small-seq models :rotating_light:

sam.r: seeing same on dashboards. p50 ~60ms, p95 ~130ms, p99 ~2100ms for small-seqs (seq=32) after deploy. throughput actually increased, so odd tail behavior — might be microbatch oscillation?

anya: profiler snapshot from a canary pod uploaded: flame graph shows long tail spent in kvcache.prefetch + fallback memcpy path. link: https://profiler.redwood/trace/ab12cd34 (internal)

alex.m: the change was enabling kv_prefetch=true and switching kernel-selector -> auto-gemm-v2 (commit f1a2b3c). autoselect seems to pick a matmul path that is fast in steady-state but terrible when microbatch fluctuates.

leo: kubectl logs -n runtime runtime-xxxx shows repeated warnings about prefetch queue saturation. snippet:
```
WARN kvcache: prefetch queue saturated (len=512)
INFO kvcache: falling back to sync fetch, duration=451ms
```

maya: traces show microbatch size oscillating between 1 and 8 within single requests — our adaptive microbatch heuristic is reacting to short bursts and causing kernel warmups then immediate fallback.

sam.r: hypothesis: prefetch assumes stable larger microbatches so it enqueues large fetches; bursts cause queue saturation and blocking -> serving threads wait on sync fetch -> p99 spike. Explains higher throughput but worse tail.

alex.m: recommend immediate rollback of kv_prefetch and pin kernel selector to v1. quick staging test: disabling prefetch drops p99 to ~180ms. @deploy-bot can we rollback canary and cancel automated promotion?

deploy-bot: Rolling back deployment/runtime to revision 2847 as requested by alex.m... rollback started.

infra-bot: Deployment rollback event: deployment/runtime rolled back by alex.m at 2026-03-17T02:18:32Z

sam.r: metrics after rollback: canary p99 back to ~190ms, prod improved within ~40s. Looks good.

anya: I'll file a bug with the profiler artifacts and add a regression test that simulates oscillating microbatch traffic. Suggest changing prefetch to safer defaults: smaller prefetch batch + aggressive drop policy when queue > 128.

alex.m: action items: 1) revert kv_prefetch default to false (PR from me), 2) add microbatch-oscillation e2e test (sam), 3) add kvcache queue saturation alert (sam), 4) postmortem draft (me).

sam.r: :thumbsup: will take 2 & 3. also adding a synthetic traffic generator with 1-8 microbatch bursts to CI.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete. All canary pods restarted. Monitoring window open 10m.

maya: thanks all. takeaway: kernel autoselect + aggressive prefetch is a throughput uplift but brittle with adaptive microbatching — need safer runtime defaults and a canary test that simulates non-steady traffic.
